reviewNotes: Reviewed the Rust 1.98.1 x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu standard-library aggregate and all sysroot license texts, including its LLVM/compiler-builtins notices; compiler implementation dependencies are excluded. Real server and TUI linker maps bind the five startup objects below. RPM ownership is glibc-devel-2.43-8.fc44.x86_64 for Scrt1.o/crti.o/crtn.o and gcc-16.2.1-2.fc44.x86_64 for crtbeginS.o/crtendS.o. The glibc SRPM fetched from https://kojipkgs.fedoraproject.org/packages/glibc/2.43/8.fc44/src/glibc-2.43-8.fc44.src.rpm contains glibc-2.43-47-gbc95068f5f.tar.xz, matching its RPM changelog (SRPM SHA-256 9a4dde3afc3d11906684d529d086cb2c060bd9c3bcf0e04f186117153dbb50f1). Its start.S, crti.S and crtn.S license headers grant unrestricted linking of their compiled versions; their exact headers are retained in legal/manual/glibc/x86_64-startup-notices.txt, with glibc LICENSES and LGPL-2.1. The Fedora patches cover localedata, CS_PATH, Python and an s390 test Makefile adjustment; none changes these startup files. GCC startup/runtime objects use GPLv3 with the supplied GCC Runtime Library Exception 3.1. The ELF executable dynamically imports the GNU loader, libc, libm and libgcc_s; these system shared libraries are not bundled and remain replaceable. Preserve the complete Rust standard-library aggregate, glibc notices and linking permission, and GCC notices/exception. This review covers only the fingerprinted Fedora 44 inputs; other toolchains or native files need review.
description: Rust 1.98.1 standard-library and Fedora 44 glibc 2.43/GCC 16.2.1 startup/runtime notices for x86_64 GNU/Linux host builds. The five listed startup objects are linked into the executable; the GNU loader, C/math runtime and GCC support shared libraries are system imports, not bundled. glibc startup files retain their linking exception and GCC runtime files retain GCC Runtime Library Exception 3.1.
